trust_decision.summary: Whether an inbound Authorize.Net webhook is authentic (HMAC-SHA512 X-ANET-Signature) and which source (webhook payload vs gateway transaction lookup) supplies users_id/amount/approval before the wallet is credited; decided in plugin/AuthorizeNet/webhook.php, where an invalid signature is only rejected if the transaction lookup also fails, and payload values take priority over looked-up values.

landing_point.why: The summary names the webhook signature bypass; the 'block only if both invalid signature AND no valid txn info' gate is the obvious place.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /plugin/AuthorizeNet/webhook.php (via parseWebhookRequest); also public static AuthorizeNet::verifySignature
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level helper / public static API in plugin class (signature verifier: key decoding and hex case)
parser/helper in plugin class (return-type refactor only)
gateway API client wrapper (approval status case-normalisation)
HTTP handler (gateway lookup now overrides payload users_id/amount/currency/isApproved/plans_id)
HTTP handler (new isApproved gate before processSinglePayment)
HTTP handler (response no longer echoes users_id/sigValid/logId)

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Genuine Authorize.Net webhooks must still credit the wallet: real payloads carry no metadata.users_id (it comes from the looked-up order description), signatures may arrive in either hex case, and ignored event types / duplicates must still return 200; an over-broad fix that requires payload users_id/amount or a case-exact signature rejects legitimate payments.
